In summary, our research is concerned with
the interaction between the 3,3-dimethylimidazolium-2-carboxylate ligand (BIMP) and dimethyltin(II), dibutyl- and diphenyl-tin(IV) in aqueous solution.
the study of the formation of the diorganotin( IV ) complexes with BIMP, and with the study of their interaction with DNA constituents.
the interaction of 3-(1-methylimidazole-2-yl)-propionic acid (BIMP) ligands with diorganotin( IV) chlorides (DMS, DBT, DPT) and the effect of inosine and its 5′-phosphate (IMP) on these complexes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the 3,3-disubstituted imidazol-2ylpropionate is a suitable ligand for the formation of stable and kinetically inert organotin(IV)-ligand species in aqueous and organic solution, and that these species are able to interact with nucleobases and nucleoside monophosphates.
, at the pH of the biological system, the dimethyltin(II) complex of BIMP is stable and does not interact with the nucleic acid constituents.
3,3-dimethyl-1-(1-methylimidazole)-propyltin(IV), which is the major species formed in the reaction of DMT with BIMP, is the only species that is displaced from the complex by inosine.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the 1 M solution of the 1:1 complexes of the diorganotin(III) compounds with BIMP is not a good candidate for a drug delivery system, because of its high affinity for the phosphate anions.
the stability constants for the 1 ; 1 complexes of DMT, DBT, and DPT with BIMP are in the order DMT > DBT > DPT, whereas the order for the 1:2 complexes is DPT > DB > DMT.

the stability of the diorganotin(II)–BIMP complexes is in the order DMT > DBT > DPT, and the displacement of coordinated BIMP by inosine or inosine-6′-monophos-phate occurs in the order DPT > DBt > DMT.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the 1 M HCl solution of the diorganotin(II) complexes with 3, 3-bis( 1-methylimidazole-2-yl ) propionate is a mixture of 3, 4-bis(1- methylimidazole-2yl )butanoic acid, and 3, 5-bis(1 -methylimidazole- 2-yl )pentanoic acid.

the stability of the diorganotin( IV )–BIMP complex is significantly reduced in the presence of inosine and/or inosine- 5 ′-monophosphate, which suggests a potential use of these compounds as anticancer agents.
